    Estimate ancestry proportions with the ADMIXTURE method

    gt_radmix.Rd

    This function estimates individual ancestry proportions (Q) and the allele frequencies of the ancestral populations (P) with the method of ADMIXTURE (Alexander et al. 2009), i.e. by maximum likelihood under the ADMIXTURE model. It uses a modified version of the algorithm of OpenADMIXTURE (Ko et al. 2023): EM priming, block-wise Newton updates solved as constrained quadratic programs, and quasi-Newton acceleration. Much of its C++ code is ported from the Julia implementation of OpenADMIXTURE, OpenADMIXTURE.jl, by Ko et al. The function has a different name because it differs from OpenADMIXTURE: it does not include the selection of ancestry informative markers (sparse K-means) that is a central part of OpenADMIXTURE; we implemented the cross-validation of ADMIXTURE, to choose K, which is not part of OpenADMIXTURE; it supports pseudohaploid data; and it changes some details of the computations (see "Differences from OpenADMIXTURE.jl" below). If you use this function, please cite Ko et al. (2023) for the algorithm, as well as Alexander et al. (2009) for the method.

    gt_radmix(
  x,
  k,
  n_runs = 1,
  seed = NULL,
  max_iter = 1000,
  rtol = 1e-07,
  n_em_iter = 5,
  n_qn = 3,
  init_q = NULL,
  init_p = NULL,
  fix_q = FALSE,
  fix_p = FALSE,
  use_imputed = FALSE,
  crossval = FALSE,
  n_folds = 5,
  n_cores = 1,
  verbose = FALSE
)

    Arguments

    x

    a tidypopgen::gen_tibble (possibly grouped)

    k

    an integer vector giving the number(s) of ancestral populations

    n_runs

    the number of runs for each value of k (defaults to 1)

    seed

    the seed for the random number generator (defaults to NULL). Either a vector of length n_runs (the same seeds are used for each k) or of length n_runs * length(k). The global random number generator state is restored on exit.

    max_iter

    the maximum number of iterations (defaults to 1000)

    rtol

    the convergence threshold on the relative change in log-likelihood between iterations (defaults to 1e-7)

    n_em_iter

    the number of EM iterations used to prime the estimates (defaults to 5)

    n_qn

    the number of secant pairs used by the quasi-Newton acceleration (defaults to 3)

    init_q

    optional matrix (individuals x k) of starting ancestry proportions; only allowed with a single value of k

    init_p

    optional matrix (loci x k) of starting allele frequencies (of the alternate allele, as in the P matrices returned by this function; those of tidypopgen::gt_admixture() give the frequency of the reference allele, so use 1 - P); only allowed with a single value of k. If it has row names (as the P matrices returned by this function), they are used to match its rows to the loci of x (it can then include other loci, which are ignored); otherwise its rows must be in the order of the loci of x

    fix_q, fix_p

    booleans; if TRUE, Q (respectively P) is kept at the value given in init_q (respectively init_p)

    use_imputed

    boolean; if TRUE, imputed genotypes are used as if they were observed; otherwise they are treated as missing (the default)

    crossval

    boolean; should the cross-validation error be computed (defaults to FALSE)? See the details.

    n_folds

    the number of folds used for cross-validation (defaults to 5, as in ADMIXTURE)

    n_cores

    the number of cores to use (defaults to 1)

    verbose

    boolean; should progress be printed (defaults to FALSE)? With verbose = TRUE, the log-likelihood is also computed (and logged) every 5 EM steps during the initial EM iterations; otherwise only their number is logged, as these values are not needed by the algorithm.

    Value

    an object of class gt_admix, a list with elements:

    • k the number of clusters of each run

    • Q a list of tidypopgen::q_matrix() objects with the ancestry proportions

    • P a list of matrices (loci x k) with the alternate allele frequencies

    • log a list with the log of each run

    • loglik the log-likelihood of each run

    • converged whether each run converged

    • cv the cross-validation error of each run (if crossval is TRUE)

    • id the id column of x

    • group the group column of x (if x is grouped)

    • algorithm "radmix"

    Details

    Genotypes are read directly from the backing file of the gen_tibble (respecting any filtering of individuals and selection of loci), so no intermediate PLINK file is written. Computation is multithreaded with OpenMP.

    Missing genotypes are ignored in the likelihood. Pseudohaploid individuals (see tidypopgen::gt_pseudohaploid()) contribute a single allele per locus. Only diploid and pseudohaploid gen_tibbles are supported.

    P gives the frequency of the alternate allele (allele_alt in tidypopgen::show_loci()) in each ancestral population.

    Supplying init_p together with fix_p = TRUE estimates the ancestry of new individuals given the allele frequencies of a reference panel (a "projection" analysis); the loci of x must then match the rows of init_p.

    Algorithm

    As in OpenADMIXTURE.jl, each run consists of:

    1. a random initialisation followed by a few EM (FRAPPE) iterations (n_em_iter);

    2. block-wise Newton updates of Q (one individual at a time, on the simplex) and P (one locus at a time, in the unit interval), each solved exactly as a small quadratic program with K. Lange's sweep-operator active-set method;

    3. quasi-Newton acceleration (Zhou, Alexander and Lange 2011) using the last n_qn secant pairs, accepted only when it improves the log-likelihood.

    Iterations stop when the relative change in log-likelihood falls below rtol. All estimates are kept within [1e-5, 1 - 1e-5], as in ADMIXTURE and OpenADMIXTURE.jl.

    Cross-validation

    With crossval = TRUE, the cross-validation error of ADMIXTURE (Alexander and Lange 2011) is computed for each run, and can be used to choose k (lower is better; see autoplot(type = "cv")). The observed genotypes are split into n_folds folds of roughly equal size; for each fold, the model is refitted with the genotypes of that fold treated as missing, and each of them is predicted by its expected value \(\mu = n \sum_k q_{ik} p_{kj}\), where \(n\) is the number of allele copies of the individual. The error is the binomial deviance $$d(g, \mu) = g \log(g / \mu) + (n - g) \log((n - g) / (n - \mu))$$ averaged over all the masked genotypes of all folds. Where ADMIXTURE does not document the details, we made the following choices:

    • each fold is fitted starting from the estimates for the full data, with the same convergence criteria (max_iter and rtol);

    • genotypes are assigned to folds by a hash of their position and of a seed drawn from the random number generator (reproducible with seed), so the folds differ from those of ADMIXTURE and the errors agree with ADMIXTURE's closely but not exactly;

    • pseudohaploid individuals use \(n = 1\).

    Cross-validation does not change the estimates of Q and P, but requires n_folds additional fits for each run (each usually converging in a few iterations).

    Comparison with ADMIXTURE

    The model and the log-likelihood are those of ADMIXTURE (Alexander et al. 2009), and the optimisation is closely related (block updates with constrained Newton steps and quasi-Newton acceleration), so both programs reach the same maximum likelihood estimates, up to local optima and the convergence tolerance. The test suite checks this on the EUR_subset data used in the OpenADMIXTURE.jl tests. Note that:

    • ADMIXTURE reports the frequency of the second allele in the PLINK bim file, which for a gen_tibble is the reference allele, so its P matrices are 1 - P of those returned here;

    • cross-validation follows ADMIXTURE (see above), and the test suite checks that the errors agree with those of ADMIXTURE on EUR_subset;

    • bootstrap standard errors and supervised analyses with individuals of known ancestry, available in ADMIXTURE, are not implemented (a fixed reference panel can be used with init_p and fix_p).

    Differences from OpenADMIXTURE.jl

    gt_radmix() uses a modified version of the algorithm of OpenADMIXTURE.jl. Starting from the same values, it reproduces the computations of OpenADMIXTURE.jl to numerical precision (this is checked by the test suite), except for the following:

    • there is no GPU (CUDA) support;

    • we implemented cross-validation, as in ADMIXTURE (see above), which is not part of OpenADMIXTURE;

    • sparse K-means selection of ancestry informative markers (SKFR) is not implemented; loci can be selected beforehand with tidypopgen::select_loci();

    • pseudohaploid individuals are supported (they contribute one allele per locus, whereas OpenADMIXTURE.jl assumes every individual is diploid);

    • with missing data, the EM update of Q is normalised by the number of loci observed in each individual (OpenADMIXTURE.jl divides by the total number of loci, so that Q is pushed off the simplex);

    • the log-likelihood is only computed when the algorithm needs it: not after each EM step (unless verbose = TRUE), and, in the main iterations, the log-likelihood after two plain updates only when the quasi-Newton step is rejected (OpenADMIXTURE.jl computes both every time). This saves about one pass over the genotypes in seven, without changing the estimates; the log then reports "basic = not computed";

    • a few numerical safeguards that the Julia code lacks: the conditioning penalty of the quadratic program for Q is never negative, the active-set solver never pivots on a vanishing element, Newton steps that are not finite are discarded (the individual or locus keeps its current value for that iteration), and the projections onto the feasible set tolerate non-finite values. None of these changes the results when the computations are well behaved; each is documented in the C++ source.

    References

    Ko S, Chu BB, Peterson D, Okenwa C, Papp JC, Alexander DH, Sobel EM, Zhou H, Lange KL (2023) Unsupervised discovery of ancestry informative markers and genetic admixture proportions in biobank-scale datasets. The American Journal of Human Genetics, 110(2), 314-325.

    Alexander DH, Novembre J, Lange K (2009) Fast model-based estimation of ancestry in unrelated individuals. Genome Research, 19(9), 1655-1664.

    Alexander DH, Lange K (2011) Enhancements to the ADMIXTURE algorithm for individual ancestry estimation. BMC Bioinformatics, 12, 246.

    Zhou H, Alexander D, Lange K (2011) A quasi-Newton acceleration for high-dimensional optimization algorithms. Statistics and Computing, 21(2), 261-273.

    Examples

    bed_file <-
  system.file("extdata", "pop_a.bed", package = "tidypopgen")
pop_a <- tidypopgen::gen_tibble(bed_file,
  backingfile = tempfile("pop_a"),
  quiet = TRUE
)
adm <- gt_radmix(pop_a, k = 2, seed = 1)
adm$Q[[1]]
#>            .Q1       .Q2
#> [1,] 0.5051543 0.4948457
#> [2,] 0.0000100 0.9999900
#> [3,] 0.9999900 0.0000100
#> [4,] 0.0000100 0.9999900
#> [5,] 0.9999900 0.0000100
#> attr(,"class")
#> [1] "q_matrix" "matrix"   "array"   

# choose k by cross-validation
adm_cv <- gt_radmix(pop_a, k = 1:3, seed = 1, crossval = TRUE)
adm_cv$cv
#> [1] 0.8224648 1.1840311 0.7096221
